title: Treasury coupon announcement (20Y bond R + 5Y TIPS R + 2Y FRN R, 13/26/6/52-week bills) — the calendar's rarest announcement shape, and the one that schedules the latest-ever December long-duration auction
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 909 tokens and 213 (security, announce, auction, settle) rows spanning 2026-08-05 to 2027-01-28 — the same 213 the 2026-11-19, 2026-12-24 and 2027-01-21 siblings derived independently, which is the parse's own cross-check. SEVEN securities carry announce date `Thursday, December 17, 2026`, read verbatim: `13-Week  BILL` and `26-Week  BILL` (auction Monday, December 21, 2026, settle Thursday, December 24, 2026), `6-Week  BILL` and `52-Week  BILL` (auction Tuesday, December 22, 2026, settle Thursday, December 24, 2026), `5-Year  TIPS` + `R` + `T` (auction Tuesday, December 22, 2026, settle Thursday, December 31, 2026), and `2-Year  FRN` + `R` and `20-Year  BOND` + `R` (both auction Wednesday, December 23, 2026, settle Monday, December 28, 2026), against the document's own legend `T --denotes TIPS`, `R --denotes reopening`. CORRECTS the count in `proposals/treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-17.from-treasury-20y-bond-2026-12-23.json`, which recorded `twelve consecutive rows` carrying this announce date; the re-derived figure is SEVEN, and its enumeration of the individual securities was otherwise correct. Stays estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the announcement's own press release on the day. The ~11:00 a.m. ET announcement slot is standing convention inherited from the sibling coupon-announcement ledgers and is NOT separately sourced; the 2026-12-24 sibling established that no Treasury dataset publishes an announcement time at all. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — the id previously existed only as TWO proposals, `proposals/treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-17.from-treasury-20y-bond-2026-12-23.json` and `proposals/treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-17.from-treasury-5y-tips-2026-12-22.json` (both 2026-09-09). BOTH were read in full first and are now shadowed; the second's composition survived the re-read intact, the first's row count did not (twelve -> seven, corrected above). WHAT MAKES THIS EVENT DIFFERENT FROM EVERY RESEARCHED SIBLING — two structural facts, both verified against the tape this session. (1) IT IS THE CALENDAR'S RAREST ANNOUNCEMENT SHAPE: three coupon legs, three different security types (nominal bond, TIPS, floating-rate note), and EVERY ONE OF THEM A REOPENING. Across 288 announcements carrying three or more coupon legs since 2015 (fiscaldata auctions_query, 1,626 clean coupon rows since 2010), exactly FOUR are all-reopening — 2020-12-17, 2021-09-16, 2022-03-17 and 2022-06-16 — so this would be the fifth and the first since June 2022. It is also the ONLY mid-month announcement in the published schedule carrying three coupon legs: 08-13, 09-10, 10-15, 11-12 and 2027-01-14 all carry exactly two (a 20-Year and a TIPS). The third leg is the 2-Year FRN, which rides the MONTH-END block in every other month of the window and migrates here in December — the mirror image of the finding the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-24 ledger made from the other side. AND 2020-12-17 IS AN EXACT STRUCTURAL TWIN: same announce date, same three legs (20-Year R, 5-Year TIPS R, 2-Year FRN R), same 12-22 TIPS auction on the same 3-business-day window — the only December instance in the record, and the single most relevant prior. (2) IT SCHEDULES THE LATEST-EVER DECEMBER LONG-DURATION AUCTION. The 20-Year reopening auctions Wednesday 2026-12-23. Across the entire 2010-2026 record NO coupon auction of any tenor longer than SEVEN YEARS has ever taken place on or after December 22 — every one of the 55 late-December coupon auctions in the census is a 2-Year, 5-Year, 7-Year, 2-Year FRN or 5-Year TIPS. The six December 20-Year auctions since the tenor's 2020 reintroduction ran 12-21, 12-21, 12-21, 12-20, 12-17 and 12-17, so 12-23 is later than any of them by two calendar days and reverses six years of drift toward earlier slots. This CONFIRMS the substance of the from-20y-bond proposal's `unprecedented date` claim on an independent re-derivation. BOTH STRUCTURAL FACTS TEST TO NULL, which is the ledger's actual verdict and the reason nothing here is a call: a compressed announce-to-auction window does not predict demand once the reopening confound is removed (naive slope t -1.03, controlled t +0.72, n=1,197), and late-December does not penalise duration (the 7-Year, the longest leg that has ever run in that window, reads z -0.240 vs +0.021, t -0.82, n=12). THE ONE LARGE AND ROBUST EFFECT IN THE DATA IS THE REOPENING PREMIUM — reopenings clear +0.367 z above same-tenor new issues (t +5.17; 20-Year +1.303 at t +6.86, 30-Year TIPS +1.448 at t +5.48, 5-Year TIPS +0.882 at t +3.09), and it is simultaneously the omitted variable that manufactured the compression story. TWO METHOD FINDINGS THIS CALENDAR'S RATES SERIES SHOULD INHERIT, both banked in the ledger: the reopening indicator is the omitted control in any auction-demand test here (within-leg corr(gap, reopening) reaches -0.72 on the 30-Year and -0.71 on the 10-Year), and fiscaldata's auctions_query contains FIVE non-scheduled same-day $25 million add-on records since 2010 (2019-06-21, 2019-12-06, 2020-07-10, 2021-12-02, 2022-07-14, bid-to-covers 3.43 / 5.40 / 6.31 / 2.92 / 5.32) which must be filtered at a $1B floor or a small sample's t-statistic is fabricated — those five alone moved the naive gap slope from t -2.26 to t -1.03. CONTENT: all three sizes are DEDUCTIONS, not published. 20-Year reopening $13B and 2-Year FRN reopening $28B follow sb0590's alternating refunding columns (re-read direct this session, HTTP 200, 75,577 bytes) plus an unbroken tape — the 20-Year has printed exactly $13B on all 18 reopenings since 2024-06 and $16B on every new issue. The 5-Year TIPS reopening at $24B is a DOUBLE deduction: sb0590's TIPS paragraph names only `the October 5-year TIPS new issue auction size at $26 billion`, and the December reopening is $2B below its own CUSIP's new issue in 31 of 33 cases since 2010 and 15 of 15 on the December leg. That gives $65B of coupons, the SMALLEST coupon announcement in the published window against 12-03's deduced $119B and 12-24's $183B. Also on the record: the 5-Year TIPS size ladder has stopped climbing — $26B new issue for three consecutive scheduled auctions (2025-10, 2026-04, guided 2026-10), the longest flat run since the $17B pause of 2019-04 to 2020-10, making Dec-2026's deduced $24B the second flat December in the record after 2020's. CORRIDOR: 26 tracked entries within +/-5 days, and it is the busiest central-bank corridor any announcement in this series has faced — boe-decision-2026-12-17 and ecb-decision-2026-12-17 land on the announcement's own day, boj-decision-2026-12-18 the next, alongside quad-witching opex-2026-12-18 and retail-sales-2026-12-16. NO NEW EVENT WAS PROPOSED IN THIS PR and that is a finding, not an omission: all three downstream auctions this announcement confirms — treasury-5y-tips-2026-12-22, treasury-20y-bond-2026-12-23 and treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23 — already exist as canonical files, and the four bill legs are deliberately not filed, since this calendar tracks no bill auction of any tenor and creating that class inside an adjacency sweep would be a scope decision rather than a discovery (the line both December siblings drew). This entry carries symbols: [] and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed; the date is estimate and nothing here licenses an entry.
